GAS: Grassroots App Store
An *identity* is a unique key pair, chosen by the person who has it.
Alice *trusts* Bob when she knows Bob personally and believes him to keep the undertakings he signs under grassroots contracts.
The *author* of an item is its first signer.
A *program* is an item: compiled code, signed by its compiler, that gives the grassroots contract it is compiled from, its clauses and its speech-act schemas; its *developer* is its author. Alice *trusts* Carol *as a developer* when she has declared it and has not withdrawn the declaration.
A *relation* is a friendship or the membership of a group. Bob *trusts* Carol, a ward of Alice, when he trusts Alice. The *decision rule*, a parameter of GnW, says who decides for a ward and how. Here: the guardians deciding jointly.
A *service* is a ward operated by a machine at an address every person can reach.
A *store* is a service holding a list of programs. Alice *trusts* a store when she has declared it and has not withdrawn the declaration.
Alice, Bob and Carol are persons. A party to a contract must have an identity. Alice and Bob are persons. Alice, Bob and Erin are persons, Carol and Dave wards. Alice is a person, Dave a service. Alice, Bob and Carol are persons, Dave a service.
GKK:1. ○ Establish: Alice may establish an identity once. Alice will make herself known by its public key, sign her acts with its private key, and be accountable for every act signed with it.
GKK:2. ■ Acquaint: Alice and Bob may jointly come to know each other.
GKK:3. ■ Introduce: Alice may introduce Carol to Bob with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other and Alice knows Carol.
GSG:1. ○ Befriend: Alice and Bob, who trust each other and are not friends, may jointly become friends.
GSG:2. ■ Unfriend: Alice may end her friendship with Bob.
GSG:3. ○ Loss of Trust. Alice will end her friendship with Bob if she ceases to trust him.
GFP:1. ■ Sign: Alice may create an item by signing it.
GFP:2. ■ Forward: Alice may forward an item she holds to her friend Bob, adding her signature to the signatures the item carries.
GPD:1. ◆ Publish: Carol may publish a program by signing it, attesting that its schemas say what its clauses say, that it is the result of compiling the schemas, and that it is expected to behave correctly according to the contract.
GPD:2. ■ Developer Trust. Trust: Alice may declare trust in Carol, whom she knows, as a developer. Untrust: Alice may withdraw the declaration.
GPD:3. ■ Offer: Carol may offer a program she holds to her friend Alice by forwarding it to her.
GPD:4. ■ Install: Alice may install a program she published, as well as a program offered to her whose developer she trusts.
GPD:5. ■ Invite: Alice may invite her friend Bob to join her in a program she installed, with the consent of Bob, who trusts its developer; Bob then has the program installed, with Alice's signature added, and each is a participant of the program with the other.
GPD:6. ■ Leave: Alice may leave a program she installed; it is then no longer installed, and her participation in it with every participant ends.
GnW:1. ■ Enter: Alice may create a ward, Carol, and establish Carol's identity by choosing Carol's key pair. Alice is then the creator, a guardian and a friend of Carol.
GnW:2. ■ Guardian decisions. Make guardian: Those who decide for Carol may make Bob a guardian and a friend of Carol, with the consent of Bob. Resign: Bob may end his guardianship of Carol. End guardian: Those who decide for Carol may end Bob's guardianship. Guardian unfriend: Bob may end his friendship with Carol, which ends his guardianship. Carol may not end a friendship with her guardian.
GnW:3. ■ Ward and person. Ward acquaint: Carol, a ward of Alice, and Bob may jointly come to know each other. Ward befriend: Carol may enter a relation with Bob with the consent of Bob and Alice, provided Carol and Bob know each other and Alice and Bob are friends. Ward end, Unfriend, Ward unfriend: Carol, Bob or Alice may end the relation of Bob and Carol.
GnW:4. ■ Wards. Wards acquaint: Carol, a ward of Alice, and Dave, a ward of Bob, may jointly come to know each other. Wards befriend: Carol may enter a relation with Dave with the consent of Dave, Alice and Bob, provided Carol and Dave know each other, Alice knows Dave and is a friend of Bob, Alice and Bob possibly one person.
GnW:5. ■ Retire: Those who decide for Carol may retire Carol; every guardianship and relation of Carol then ends and Carol can take no act.
GAS:1. ■ Open store: Carol may make her service Dave a store.
GAS:2. ○ Listing. List: Carol may list in Dave a program developed by Bob, after adding her signature to its signatures, provided she trusts Bob as a developer. Delist: Carol may delist it. Carol will delist it if she ceases to trust Bob as a developer.
GAS:3. ■ Store trust. Trust store: Alice may declare trust in Dave, Carol being known to her. Untrust store: Alice may withdraw the declaration.
GAS:4. ■ Install from store: Alice may install a program listed in a store she trusts.
